➡️From Vintage to MNTGE: Digital Fashion Brand to Release NFT Patches Linked to IRL Rewards

Digital fashion brand MNTGE is gearing up to release its Patchwork collection, comprised of a series of non-fungible token (NFT) patches paired with a physical counterpart.

MNTGE Patchwork features 13 unique digital patches designed by 11 artists including Jen Stark, Bored Ape Yacht Club artist Seneca and Nyan Cat meme creator Christopher Torres. The entire 7,500-unit collection will open for sale on July 27 on NFT marketplace OpenSea. Each NFT will be priced at 0.07 ETH, or $130, and the artwork will be revealed upon mint.

Each NFT is linked to an identical physical patch. Embedded with a near-field communication (NFC) chip, owners can scan the real-world patch to claim the digital token in their crypto wallet. By holding the patch on the blockchain and IRL, users can trace ownership as well as attend token-gated events and exclusive MNTGE experiences.

Additionally, the patches aren’t just one-off collectibles. In the physical world, they can be sewn onto MNTGE’s “base garments,” including t-shirts, jackets and denim. In the digital realm, the patches can be “owned” by the base garment itself. By implementing an ERC-6551 token standard, the digital wearable becomes a token-bound account that can custody the patches – creating an added layer of digital ownership.

Nick Adler, co-founder of MNTGE, told CoinDesk that the company was rooted in the goal of selling vintage fashion and utilizing the blockchain to revitalize its origins.

“People are out there wearing [vintage] and collecting it…young kids want to be authentic,” said Adler. “They don't want a Hot Topic shirt, they want the original shirt, right? So we just saw this natural, really honest use case for the blockchain, and we just felt like the two could really go hand in hand.”

TON DNS Summer (Part 1)

As we predicted, the hype around TON DNS has begun. The hype began with Four-Digit domains (hereinafter referred to as 4N domains). People are "burning" their 100 TON on the TON DNS smart contract and transferring this value to NFTs (similar to Banksy's work). 

On February 13, the last domain from the Club 100 (0074.ton), was minted, on February 17, the thousandth domain (5755.ton), and on February 28, the last domain from the 1k Club (0863.ton).

The race is on, and people have already minted many beautiful numbers from various masks and special collections, although only 26% of the total supply has been minted.

On average, 117 4N domains are minted per day. At the current rate, 50% of the supply will be minted by March 22, 2026, 75% by April 12, 2026, and 100% by May 4, 2026. 

Why 4N domains if there are already Telegram usernames?

1. Numbers are the international language of communication. They are simple and understandable for everyone around the world, unlike various alphabets (be it Latin, Cyrillic, Arabic, hieroglyphs, etc.).

2. There are 10^4 = 10,000 number combinations in 4N domains, compared to 26^4 = 456,976 combinations in alphabetical ones.

3. The price for the 4L username is fixed at $8,000. The price for the 4N domain on mint is approximately $130, which is 61.54 times cheaper!

4. Only domains can consist of numbers, while usernames must contain at least one letter. Therefore, 4N domains are beyond competition in the TON ecosystem.

5. The ability to associate attractive domain digits with a gift number. An example is here. There are dozens of different collections of gifts with identical numbers, but only one 4N domain can be associated with them!

6. The TON ecosystem will have thousands of AI agents, and they will need a short digital domain for convenience.

7. TON Browser and TON Messenger are being developed, with user login via TON DNS.

8. Repeating the success of ENS, this time in the form of a utility — a shell in Telegram (because TON DNS renewal costs pennies, compared to $160 per year for a 4-digit ENS).

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei has rejected criticism that announcing a joint meeting between Iran and the Persian Gulf states contributed to a decline in global oil prices, saying diplomatic decisions cannot be made based on a single factor and that the priority is to secure national interests at the appropriate time.

Responding to criticism that the meeting should have been postponed because the announcement weakened pressure on Iran’s enemies, Baqaei said, “With this kind of approach, one can always argue that now is not the time for a particular diplomatic action.”
​
“You cannot make decisions in the field of diplomacy and seize opportunities based solely on one factor and one consideration; what ultimately matters to us is securing national interests at the appropriate time,” he added in his interview with national television.
​
The spokesperson said the diplomatic engagement with regional countries should be viewed in the broader context of Iran’s security and foreign-policy objectives.
​
“In such circumstances, when apparently no movement should have taken place, the fact that our diplomacy succeeds, backed by the power of the field, in bringing countries to the conclusion that the solution to common security in the region is to sit together and engage in dialogue without the presence of foreigners is not a small achievement,” Baqaei said.
​
Baqaei also rejected the description of Iran’s current situation as one of “neither war nor peace,” saying the country is actually in a state of war.
​
“We are in a state of war. The reason is clear. As long as economic sanctions and the naval blockade by the enemy continue, economic war also continues, and this constitutes war,” he said.
​
Referring to UN General Assembly Resolution 3314, Baqaei said an economic or naval blockade of a country is considered an act of aggression under international law. “Therefore, whatever we do in this situation is called defense,” he said.
​
On repeated US accusations that Iran is involved in Yemen, the spokesperson described the allegations as a recurring pattern in US policymaking, saying Washington was attempting to attribute its own mistakes and problems to others.
​
He said such an approach would not resolve the problems but would instead mislead public opinion and prevent the United States itself from finding solutions.
​
Baqaei said the wrong accusations against Iran showed that Washington’s objective was to further destabilize the situation and maintain turmoil among Muslim countries.
​
He added that Iran was ready to help facilitate dialogue and implement a roadmap agreed upon by the Yemenis and relevant parties, including Saudi Arabia, stressing that Tehran’s position was principled and based on what the parties themselves had agreed.

Tesla will release a “human” for $20,000

Musk officially confirmed: the first Optimus robots will go on sale in 2027.

And the bet on them is so massive that, to make room for these robots, the company has already discontinued its legendary Model S and Model X cars.

Tesla wants to create a truly universal assistant: clean the house, put things away, bring in groceries, load the washing machine, open the door, use regular tools, and learn new tasks simply by being told what to do.

In short, a new member of the family for every household. And on top of that, a universal worker in any factory.

The target price is around $20–30K, although Tesla has not announced the final price yet.

Right now, in Texas, they are designing a factory to produce 10 million robots a year. That’s 20 times more than the number of robots being made worldwide right now.

So Tesla is going almost all-in on this field.

Although the bet is worth it. If Optimus learns to work like a human, for the first time, the workforce could simply be produced on an assembly line. And here’s a solution to demographic problems around the world.
